You can automatically delete messages from a sender based upon their email address by using Thunderbird's Message Filters feature. This article describes what they are and how to use them:

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/organize-your-messages-using-filters

Your email provider probably has similar filtering and blocking features, accessible on their webmail page. The advantage of doing it there is that the problem will be taken care of even before Thunderbird can download it.

content:
Is this an Oauth2 account, or POP3?

What is your operating system?

What is your default web browser?

Please show us a screen shot of the error message.

This error usually happens when cookies are not enabled in Thunderbird. The fix is to enable that setting (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content>) and make sure the "Accept cookies from sites" option is checked; also delete any cookies for Google/Gmail ( <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites | Show Cookies>.) ALSO, delete your currently saved passwords, as described above by Joel. Then restart Thunderbird and you should be prompted for your new credentials.

Of course, this depends on you being able to start Thunderbird so you can get at its settings. That's why I want to see a screen shot. You're describing the browser window that normally pops up during Oauth2 authorization so you can input your credentials, but I've never seen such a window that you can't either dismiss or move aside.
